ruling.recommended_action: Refund the $6.61 no-show cancellation fee to the rider as a Ryde voucher (NS-7) and send the driver's account to Ryde review for the arrival-button tap recorded 351 m from the pickup point + flag_account
ruling.reasoning: The cancellation was made by the driver, so the fee can only stand through NS-1 [F3][NS-0]. Ryde's own rule makes arrival and waiting conditional: the "I'm Here" tap must be at the pickup location and the driver must then remain there continuously for more than three minutes [F5][NS-1]. The trace settles both spatial elements against the driver: at the 08:47:20 tap he was 351 m from the pickup point, and his closest approach during the whole episode was 319 m, never once inside the 200 m radius [F5][F1][NS-1]. He then stayed inside the radius for 0 seconds after the tap, his 4 min 0 s stationary period being spent 350 m away [F5][F2][NS-1]. The rider was entitled to stay where she was: she was at the pickup point and said so at 08:48, whereas the driver's 08:47 "Reached already" message was inaccurate on his own GPS record [F9][F8][F2][NS-1]. The driver's post-hoc statement that he "pressed I'm Here and waited more than 3 minutes at the pickup" is a claim, not consent or proof of place, and it is overridden by the location records [F12][F5][F2][NS-1]. With NS-1 (ii) and (iii) both failing, the $6.61 fee is not chargeable and must be returned in full [F3][F6][NS-2][NS-7]. The amount is the recorded cancellation fee of $6.61, itemised on the fare record and matching the published figure, with no surge applied [F6][F7][NS-2]. Separately, a tap on the arrival button while GPS places the driver outside the pickup radius is the abuse-of-cancellation-button conduct Ryde treats as fraudulent, so the case carries a flag_account referral [F5][F1][NS-2]. Profile facts are not used to decide the fee, and the driver's otherwise clean history does not change the recorded tap location [F17][F16][NS-2].

rejected_claims.reason: The mere existence of the tap at 08:47:20 is recorded [F5], but NS-1(i) is only one element; the tap must be coupled with the driver being at the pickup location, and the record shows 351 m at the tap and a closest approach of 319 m [F5][F1][NS-1].
Duration alone does not satisfy NS-1(iii): the 4 min 0 s stationary period was spent 350 m from the pickup point, with 0 s inside the radius after the tap [F2][F5][NS-1].

The rider did show up; she messaged that she was at the pickup point at 08:48 with no car there, while the driver's 08:47 arrival message was contradicted by his own recorded position 350 m away [F9][F8][F2][NS-1].

Fair weather and the absence of incidents or congestion remove any excuse for not reaching the bay; they do not convert a stationary position 350 m away into the pickup point [F15][F13][F14][F2][NS-1].
The $6.61 figure is the ordinary published fee and is not disputed on arithmetic [F6][F7], but NS-0 and NS-2 make the fee conditional on NS-1 being satisfied, which it is not [F3][NS-0][NS-2].
Profile facts cannot decide the fee or block the account referral; the driver's 992 trips and 0 disputes do not cure the recorded 351 m tap [F17][F5][NS-2].

Accepted in substance: the rider's 08:48 message places her at the pickup point and the driver's arrival message was false on GPS [F9][F8][F2]; the driving conduct is otherwise not in issue, so no separate point turns on this claim beyond NS-1.
Withdrawn by the rider advocate; the account flag rests on the recorded tap location, not on profile facts, and profiles are not used to decide the case [F5][F4][F17][NS-2].
Traffic and weather facts bear on reroute justification (RD-4), which is not the dispute here; they neither support nor defeat the no-show fee [F13][F14][F15][NS-1].
